blurb: From the Quranic revelation in 7th-century Arabia through caliphates, scholarship, and Sufism to a world religion of nearly two billion.

events.description: Muslims believe Muhammad receives the first revelation in 610 near Mecca and preaches one God; the messages, recited until his death in 632, become the Quran.
events.title: Muhammad & the Quranic revelation

events.description: Muhammad and his followers emigrate to Medina in 622 — year one of the Islamic calendar — and form a community joining worship, law, and governance.
events.title: The Hijra & the Medina community

events.description: Under Caliph Uthman, an authoritative text of the Quran is produced and variant codices ordered destroyed — fixing the scripture's consonantal form.
events.title: The Quran standardized

events.description: Civil wars over succession to Muhammad culminate in the killing of his grandson Husayn at Karbala (680) — the founding trauma of Shia Islam and its split from the Sunni majority.
events.title: First Fitna & Karbala — the Sunni–Shia divide

events.description: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik builds the Dome of the Rock on the site associated with the Prophet's Night Journey — Islam's oldest major monument, its walls inscribed with Quranic verses.
events.title: Dome of the Rock, Jerusalem

events.description: Scholars compile vast verified collections of the Prophet's sayings (al-Bukhari's Sahih, c. 870), while Abbasid Baghdad's translation movement advances mathematics, medicine, and philosophy.
events.title: Hadith collections & the Baghdad Golden Age

events.description: Mystical Sufism becomes Islam's great devotional current; Jalal al-Din Rumi's Masnavi — tens of thousands of couplets on divine love — is among the most-read poems in the world.
events.title: Sufism flowers — Rumi

events.description: The Ottomans take Constantinople (1453) and, ruling most of the Middle East and the Balkans, style their sultans caliphs; Sinan's mosques define classical Islamic architecture.
events.title: Ottoman caliphate & classical Islam

events.description: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab's pact with the Saudi house (1744) launches a puritan reform calling Islam back to Quran and Sunna alone — influential far beyond Arabia through later Saudi patronage.
events.title: The Wahhabi reform movement

events.description: Ayatollah Khomeini's revolution makes Iran a Shia Islamic republic governed by clerics — a landmark of modern political Islam, with echoes across the Muslim world.
events.title: The Iranian Revolution

name: Islam
